title: Mom said her son was a genius
author: Storytime
hook: A mom emailed me every week saying her son was a genius and I was failing him. Then he turned in his essay.
story: I teach eighth grade English. This year I have a student, Tyler. Sweet kid. Average grades. His mom, though, emails me every single Friday. Tyler is gifted. Tyler is bored. Tyler deserves an A. I always reply politely. Then last month, Tyler's essays got perfect. Like, college level. Vocabulary I'd never heard from him. I was honestly impressed. Until I got to the last paragraph of his essay about summer vacation. It said, as a mother of three, I've learned that summers go by too fast. Tyler is the oldest of three. He is thirteen. His mom had been writing his homework. And she forgot to change the last paragraph. I didn't say anything. I just asked Tyler to stay after class and write a short paragraph about his summer. In front of me. He looked at the paper for five minutes. Then he wrote, my mom does my homework because she wants me to get into a good school. I'm not allowed to tell. He looked terrified. Now his mom has requested a parent-teacher conference tomorrow, to discuss why Tyler only got a B. How do I handle this?
caption: as a mother of three... 📝 #storytime
sound: a light, curious piano with a funny twist at very low volume
why: School and parent stories go viral constantly, the suddenly perfect essays are the setup, the mother of three line is a funny reveal, and the conference question invites advice.

title: Siblings voted me to host Christmas
author: Storytime
hook: My siblings voted for me to host Christmas this year. Then I found out what else they had voted on.
story: Three years ago, my parents wanted to downsize. So I bought their house from them. Market price, a real mortgage, everything official. My older brother and sister were living in other states, and they never asked about it. Last week, our sibling group chat lit up. They had voted. I'm hosting Christmas, because I have the family house and the most space. Fine. I love Christmas. Then my sister accidentally sent a message meant for my brother. It said, perfect, once everyone's there, we'll bring up selling the house and splitting it three ways. Mom and Dad can't say no in front of everyone. They thought I got the house for free. That I was living in their inheritance. They had a whole plan. My brother was going to bring printed valuations. I called my parents. My dad laughed so hard he had to sit down. Then he said, bring them. And bring your mortgage statements. All of them. So on Christmas Eve, I'll have the turkey, the tree, and a folder with thirty-six monthly payments in my name. My wife thinks I should just tell them now and avoid the drama. Should I?
caption: I'll bring the turkey AND the paperwork 🎄 #storytime
sound: a cheerful Christmas jingle that turns slightly ominous at very low volume
why: Holiday family plans are peaking, siblings plotting over a house is a classic money drama, the accidental message is the twist, and the tell them now or wait question splits the comments.

title: I returned my own Christmas present
author: Storytime
hook: I found an expensive designer bag hidden in our closet. It wasn't my style, so I assumed it wasn't for me. I returned it.
story: My husband Ben is terrible at hiding things. Last week I was looking for wrapping paper and found a shopping bag behind his suits. Inside was a designer handbag. Bright pink. Over a thousand dollars. I don't wear pink. I don't even like designer bags. And Ben knows that. His coworker Sasha, though, posts pictures of pink bags every week. Ben had been working late a lot. I didn't sleep that night. The next morning, while he was at work, I took the bag back to the store, with the receipt that was inside. Got a full refund. Then I sat in my car and cried. That evening Ben came home, went straight to the closet, and his face went white. He said, where is it? I said, ask Sasha. He looked so confused. Then he pulled out his phone and showed me a message from my mom. Two months old. It said, Ben, I know she says she hates pink, but she's wanted that exact bag since high school. It was her dream bag. Trust me. My mom was right. I did want it. I just never told anyone, even Ben. And now it's sold out everywhere. How do I fix this?
caption: it was my dream bag the whole time 💗 #storytime
sound: a soft, slightly sad holiday piano at very low volume
why: Gift season and Black Friday are coming, the not my style detail misleads viewers like it misled her, the mom's message is the twist, and how do I fix this invites lots of advice.
